paths.title: Prepare infrastructure for devices using Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Entra ID
paths.summary: Learn how to configure Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Intune to support modern endpoint management. This learning path covers identity infrastructure, device enrollment, and automated deployment strategies for Windows, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Android devices.

modules.title: Understand endpoint management strategies and Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Introduces Microsoft Intune, management models (cloud-only, hybrid, co-managed), and how Microsoft Entra ID supports device management.
modules.tldr: Intune is Microsoft's cloud service for managing devices (MDM) and protecting data inside apps (MAM). Microsoft Entra ID supplies the user, group and device identities that every Intune assignment depends on. Pick a management model — cloud-only, hybrid or co-managed — based on your existing infrastructure and migration goals.
objectives: Describe how Microsoft Intune works as a cloud-based device management service
Compare Configuration Manager, Intune and co-management
Explain the role of Microsoft Entra ID in Intune-based device management
Evaluate cloud-only, hybrid and co-managed device management models
Identify the key MDM capabilities in Intune
keyPoints: **MDM** manages the whole device (settings, updates, security, inventory); **MAM** protects corporate data inside apps and also works on devices that are **not enrolled** — ideal for BYOD.
Policies are created in the **Intune admin center**, assigned to **Entra ID groups**, and delivered to devices over **HTTPS** — no VPN or on-premises servers needed.
Intune **can't work without Microsoft Entra ID**: enrollment starts with Entra authentication and creates a device object Intune references.

Three join types: **Entra registered** (BYOD, light management via app protection), **Entra joined** (cloud-only corporate, full MDM), **hybrid Entra joined** (also in on-prem AD, enables co-management).
**Co-management** = one Windows device managed by Configuration Manager *and* Intune; you move **workloads** (e.g. compliance, Windows Update policies) to Intune one at a time.
**RBAC** limits what each admin sees and can do — e.g. help desk can wipe a lost device without seeing licensing.
Intune supports the full device lifecycle: **provision → configure → secure → monitor → retire**.

units.title: What is Microsoft Intune and how does it work?
points: Cloud service: configuration and policy definitions live in the cloud; devices check in over the internet.
MDM controls the device; MAM protects data in apps, also on unenrolled devices. Many organizations combine both (corporate phones enrolled, personal tablets app protection only).
On enrollment the device registers and downloads a management profile that establishes trust.
Intune tracks compliance, reports inventory and can run remote actions such as lock or wipe.
Typical roles: Global Administrator, Intune Administrator (no billing/licensing), and a compliance-focused admin role; RBAC narrows permissions per job.

units.title: Compare Configuration Manager, Intune, and co-management
points: Configuration Manager: on-premises, Windows-focused, deep inventory and scripting, works offline — but needs servers and bandwidth.
Intune: cloud, multi-platform (Windows, macOS, iOS/iPadOS, Android), modern app types (Win32, MSIX, Store) — less granular inventory, needs internet.
Co-management: Windows 10/11 only; phased migration per workload; extra complexity of dual management.
To start: enroll a Configuration Manager–managed device in Intune, then in the Configuration Manager console choose which workloads Intune controls.

units.title: Understand the role of Microsoft Entra ID in Intune
points: Every Intune assignment is identity-based: users, groups and devices come from Entra ID.
The device object records type, ownership and join type.
Entra ID issues the tokens; Conditional Access combines identity with device compliance from Intune before granting access.

units.title: Evaluate device management models
points: **Cloud-only**: devices Entra joined, all policy from Intune — for cloud-first, remote/mobile and BYOD scenarios.
**Hybrid**: devices joined to on-prem AD and hybrid Entra joined; Group Policy and Intune side by side — for legacy apps that need domain authentication.
**Co-managed**: Configuration Manager and Intune together, shifting workloads gradually — for heavy Configuration Manager users.
You can start with one model and evolve as the organization changes.

units.title: Explore MDM capabilities in Intune
points: Enrollment and provisioning: Autopilot, Apple automated enrollment, or manual enrollment; zero-touch setup reduces hands-on work.
Configuration profiles set device settings; security baselines give recommended settings; compliance policies check requirements and can flag or block non-compliant devices.
App deployment (store, line-of-business, web apps), monitoring and reporting dashboards, and remote actions (lock, wipe, reset).

keyTerms.definition: Mobile device management — settings and policies applied to an enrolled device.
Mobile application management — protects corporate data inside apps; works without enrollment.
Configuration Manager and Intune manage the same Windows device; workloads are switched to Intune individually.
A management area (e.g. compliance policies, Windows Update policies) assigned to either Configuration Manager or Intune under co-management.

keyTerms.term: Microsoft Entra registered / joined / hybrid joined
keyTerms.definition: The three device identity types: personal (BYOD), cloud-only corporate, and on-prem AD–joined with a cloud identity.

tables.title: Which management model?
rows: Cloud-first, remote workforce, minimal on-prem infrastructure, BYOD
Hybrid Microsoft Entra joined (on-prem AD + Entra)
Existing AD investment, legacy apps needing domain authentication, Group Policy still required
Large Configuration Manager estates migrating workload by workload

remember: BYOD without enrollment → think **MAM / app protection policies**, not MDM.
Co-management is **Windows only**; macOS, iOS/iPadOS and Android are managed by Intune alone.
Intune policies target **Entra ID groups** — no group, no assignment.

selfCheck.q: Employees want to read company email on their personal phones without enrolling them. Which Intune approach fits?
selfCheck.a: MAM — app protection policies protect the corporate data in the apps without enrolling the device.

selfCheck.q: A company manages 10,000 laptops with Configuration Manager and wants to move compliance to the cloud first. What do they enable?
selfCheck.a: Co-management, switching the compliance policies workload to Intune while Configuration Manager keeps the rest.

selfCheck.q: Which device join type is used for cloud-only corporate devices with full MDM?
